title: The statistical allowance of 0.45 epsilon is adjustable
live_status: partial. Three mathematical allocation rows exist and the original split is retained.
optimistic_max_factor: <1.1x. One-sided, quantum gains at most (epsilon - b_Q)/(0.45 epsilon) = 1.77-2.18x fewer calls. A fair comparison also gives classical its best share (e_C ~ 0.99 epsilon; exact-date float64 RQMC has negligible bias), which gains (2.2)^p_C = 2.2-4.5x. The net factor is 0.39-0.99, i.e. worse for quantum for p_C in [1, 1.9]. B8 at $0.001 has no feasible quantum share at all (bias 1.24 epsilon).
cheapest_decisive_test: Two-sided allocation algebra, already done here at zero cost. The ratio change is (e_Q/0.45eps)/(e_C/0.45eps)^p_C <= (e_C/0.45eps)^(1-p_C) <= 1 whenever e_Q <= e_C and p_C >= 1. Measured inputs: biases from the G2 ledger; p_C 0.99-1.04 for smooth payoffs and 1.58-1.90 for the knock-out.
kill_or_defer_criterion: Kill now as a quantum lever: under fair two-sided allocation it cannot improve the inequality. Reopen only if some case has measured p_C < 1 (none observed), or to minimise an already-certified T_Q once an advantage is otherwise within 2x. Fold any residual work into E24.
notes: Near-duplicate of E24 ('Optimize the error split only over supported certificates'; E24 already holds 6 allocation rows). The Stage C spec already labels the 0.45 epsilon classical share as quantum-favourable. Its e_C = 0.9 epsilon sensitivity row makes classical 3.4x (B4) and 4.3x (B8) faster, so the primary decision row flatters quantum by roughly 1.5-2.5x net of any quantum reallocation.

title: Fitted convergence exponents are not lower bounds
optimistic_max_factor: 1.1-2x on T_C at the fixed epsilon grid. Stage C has measured preint T_C at all four epsilons, so exponent uncertainty only enters interpolation or extrapolation (+/-0.15 in p_C over one decade is about 1.4x). For a frontier crossover statement the sensitivity is extreme: the epsilon reduction needed to close a 2,000x gap is 2000^(1/(p_C-1)), about 4.6e3 for p_C-1 = 0.9 and about 5e5 for p_C-1 = 0.58.
cheapest_decisive_test: Scramble-unit bootstrap of the existing Stage C C1 rate data (32 scrambles) and the C2/C5/C7 fits, with no new paths or timing. Report a CI on p_C per payoff and case, using the preregistered fit windows [8,17], [10,17] and [12,17]. It is decisive for the 'room grows like epsilon^-(p_C-1)' sentence: a CI lower bound of p_C-1 > 0.3 keeps it, and a CI that includes ~0 kills it.
kill_or_defer_criterion: Run it only if the frontier paper states an epsilon-extrapolated crossover or an epsilon^-(p_C-1) room claim; the fixed-epsilon negative needs only the measured T_C. Never acquire new timings for it. The Stage C item C8 out-of-sample run (sealed FAILED, deadline expired) stays cut.
notes: Near-duplicate of F01 ('Keep measured classical slopes inside their validated range'). Merge them; F01's next-size B4x12 development batch is optional.

title: Modelled classical time is not a timed successful price
live_status: ready. Stage C C4, C5 and C7 timing are complete. Measured preint confirmations: B4 $0.01 0.124 s and $0.001 2.688 s; B8 $0.01 0.554 s and $0.001 22.53 s. The C7 targets are fitted from 3 warm runs. Stage C item C8 v3 is sealed FAILED: the outside-CPU guard tripped and the deadline expired. 99% true-price delivery is unproved on the classical side too.
optimistic_max_factor: 1.1-2x under the current practice convention: completing confirmations or out-of-sample runs moves T_C by tens of percent. A symmetric distribution-free 99% convention would shift the net up to ~2-5x in quantum's favour. Classical would become ~10-50x slower (Maurer-Pontil plain MC, compiled) and quantum would need ~10-20x more calls (bounded AE on the $40 range with pi and log(1/delta) constants). The archived-grid minimum oracle/D_max of 16.8 stays >1 under either convention.
cheapest_decisive_test: Envelope from the existing C2 confirmation runs (16 scramble means, hw99) with no new timings. (a) Practice convention: take the measured T_C as is. (b) Symmetric-rigor convention: inflate T_C to a distribution-free 99% classical procedure, inflate quantum calls to rigorous bounded AE, and recompute the min-grid oracle/D_max. If it stays >10 at t_layer >= 100 ns for every k >= 1 under both conventions (expected: >= ~34), the negative result needs no further C09 work.
kill_or_defer_criterion: Freeze full G4 until the quantum side has a compiled complete per-call depth within ~30x of D_max: no C8 relaunch, no GPU or plain-MC anchors, no 20-run confirmations for the C7 targets. Do not retry the noise-guarded C8. Timing precision of +/-10% is irrelevant against a gap of at least 17x, realistically at least 10^3. The full G4 run is needed only for an advantage claim.
notes: The negative result needs only an upper envelope on the time of a valid 99% classical price, and the coverage standard must be symmetric with the quantum side. The coverage convention is the one C-family input that can move the inequality by more than 2x. Overlaps G4 and the F-family classical comparator items.

title: A classical cubic exponent is not necessary for a crossover
live_status: audit, not started (about 80% of the content already exists in results/frontier_classical_20261001/decision_interim_v2)

Zero-cost screen inputs: accepted A10 depths with per-call = 2 x forward (B4 1.11M, B8 1.33M), measured preint T_C, sigma_Q and e = 0.45 epsilon. Over epsilon in {0.1, 0.03, 0.01, 0.001}, k in {1, 3, 10} and t_layer in {10 ns, 100 ns, 1 us, 10 us}, the minimum oracle/D_max is 16.8 (B8, $0.1 with setup-dominated T_C, k=1, 10 ns). So there is no tenfold and no break-even anywhere on the archived grid. Primary corner (k=3, 100 ns, $0.001): B4 15,600x, B8 2,040x. A realistic 1-10 us t_layer adds 10-100x.
cheapest_decisive_test: Rerun the grid above in the decision_interim_v2 conventions with the A10 depths, add the reflection cost, and label each input as observed, modelled or extrapolated. Run it under both coverage conventions from C09. This decides the scoped negative now.
kill_or_defer_criterion: If min oracle/D_max > 10 at every corner with t_layer >= 100 ns (expected), publish the scoped result 'no tenfold, and no break-even, for this construction'. Then move spend from certification items to levers with >10x optimistic potential: A-family depth floors and reformulation, F-family reformulation, H-family t_layer. Revisit only when a lever's optimistic product brings some corner to <= 10.
notes: The single most valuable C item. Epsilon = $0.001 is the most quantum-favourable epsilon (p_C > 1), except where loose-epsilon T_C is setup-dominated.
